title: Book of Leviticus (Chapter 19, Verses 1–2)
text: The LORD spoke unto Moses, saying, Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.

title: Book of Leviticus (Chapter 19, Verses 9–10)
text: When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corners of your field, neither shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest. You shall not glean your vineyard, neither shall you gather every grape of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and the stranger: I am the LORD your God.

title: Book of Leviticus (Chapter 19, Verses 11–12)
text: You shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another. You shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shall you profane the name of your God: I am the LORD.

title: Book of Leviticus (Chapter 19, Verses 13–14)
text: You shall not defraud your neighbor, neither rob him. The wages of him that is hired shall not remain with you all night until the morning. You shall not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind, but shall fear your God: I am the LORD.

title: Book of Leviticus (Chapter 19, Verses 15–16)
text: You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment. You shall not respect the person of the poor, nor honor the person of the mighty; but in righteousness shall you judge your neighbor. You shall not go up and down as a talebearer among your people, neither shall you stand against the blood of your neighbor: I am the LORD.

title: Book of Leviticus (Chapter 19, Verses 17–18)
text: You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him. You shall not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.

title: Book of Leviticus (Chapter 19, Verses 32–34)
text: You shall rise up before the gray head, and honor the face of the old man, and fear your God: I am the LORD. If a stranger sojourn with you in your land, you shall not vex him. The stranger that dwells with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.

title: Book of Leviticus (Chapter 19, Verses 35–36)
text: You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in measures of length, in weight, or in quantity. Just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin, shall you have: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.

title: Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 6, Verses 4–9)
text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one. You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might. These words, which I command you this day, shall be in your heart. You shall teach them diligently unto your children, and shall speak of them when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up.

title: Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 10, Verses 12–13)
text: And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God require of you, but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, to keep the commandments of the LORD and his statutes, which I command you this day for your good?

title: Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 10, Verses 17–19)
text: The LORD your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, mighty and terrible, who regards not persons, nor takes reward. He executes judgment for the fatherless and widow, and loves the stranger, giving him food and raiment. Love therefore the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.

title: Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 15, Verses 7–8)
text: If there be among you a poor man of one of your brethren within any of your gates in your land which the LORD your God gives you, you shall not harden your heart, nor shut your hand from your poor brother. But you shall open your hand wide unto him, and shall surely lend him sufficient for his need.

title: Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 15, Verses 10–11)
text: You shall surely give him, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give unto him; because for this thing the LORD your God shall bless you in all your works. For the poor shall never cease out of the land; therefore I command you, saying, You shall open your hand wide unto your brother, to your poor, and to your needy in your land.

title: Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 16, Verses 16–17)
text: Three times in a year shall all your males appear before the LORD your God in the place which he shall choose: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles. They shall not appear before the LORD empty; every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the LORD your God which he has given you.

title: Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 16, Verses 18–20)
text: Judges and officers shall you make in all your gates, and they shall judge the people with just judgment. You shall not wrest judgment; you shall not respect persons, neither take a gift, for a gift blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous. Justice, justice shall you pursue, that you may live and inherit the land which the LORD your God gives you.

title: Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 24, Verses 17–18)
text: You shall not pervert the judgment of the stranger, nor of the fatherless, nor take a widow's garment as pledge. But you shall remember that you were a bondman in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from there; therefore I command you to do this thing.

title: Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 24, Verses 19–22)
text: When you cut down your harvest in your field, and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you shall not go again to fetch it. It shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow, that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands. When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the boughs again. When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean it afterward. It shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.

title: Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 25, Verses 13–16)
text: You shall not have in your bag diverse weights, a great and a small. You shall not have in your house diverse measures, a great and a small. But you shall have a perfect and just weight, a perfect and just measure shall you have, that your days may be lengthened in the land which the LORD your God gives you. For all that do such things, and all that do unrighteously, are an abomination unto the LORD your God.

title: Book of Numbers (Chapter 6, Verses 24–26)
text: The LORD bless you, and keep you. The LORD make his face shine upon you, and be gracious unto you. The LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.

title: Book of Isaiah (Chapter 1, Verses 16–17)
text: Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil; learn to do well. Seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.

title: Book of Isaiah (Chapter 56, Verse 7)
text: Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon my altar; for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.

title: Book of Jeremiah (Chapter 7, Verses 3–7)
text: Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: Amend your ways and your doings, and I will cause you to dwell in this place. Trust not in lying words, saying, The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD. If you thoroughly amend your ways and your doings, if you thoroughly execute judgment between a man and his neighbor, if you oppress not the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, and shed not innocent blood in this place, then will I cause you to dwell in this land.

title: Book of Hosea (Chapter 6, Verse 6)
text: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.

title: Book of Amos (Chapter 5, Verses 21–24)
text: I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not delight in your solemn assemblies. Though you offer me burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept them. Take away from me the noise of your songs; for I will not hear the melody of your instruments. But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

title: Book of Micah (Chapter 6, Verses 6–8)
text: With what shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the high God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old? Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil? He has shown you, O man, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you, but to do justice, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

title: Book of Psalms (Psalm 15)
text: LORD, who shall abide in your tabernacle? Who shall dwell in your holy hill? He that walks uprightly, and works righteousness, and speaks the truth in his heart. He that does not backbite with his tongue, nor does evil to his neighbor, nor takes up a reproach against his neighbor. He that swears to his own hurt, and changes not. He that puts not out his money to usury, nor takes reward against the innocent. He that does these things shall never be moved.

title: Book of Psalms (Psalm 24, Verses 3–5)
text: Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? Or who shall stand in his holy place? He that has clean hands and a pure heart, who has not lifted up his soul unto vanity, nor sworn deceitfully. He shall receive blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.

title: Book of Psalms (Psalm 51, Verses 16–17)
text: You desire not sacrifice, else would I give it; you delight not in burnt offering. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.

title: Book of Psalms (Psalm 84, Verses 1–4)
text: How lovely are your dwellings, O LORD of hosts. My soul longs, yes, even faints for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God. Blessed are they that dwell in your house; they will still be praising you.

title: Book of Psalms (Psalm 122, Verses 1–6)
text: I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD. Our feet shall stand within your gates, O Jerusalem. Jerusalem is built as a city compact together, where the tribes go up, the tribes of the LORD, unto the testimony of Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the LORD. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem; they shall prosper that love you.

title: Book of Proverbs (Chapter 3, Verses 27–28)
text: Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it. Say not unto your neighbor, Go, and come again, and tomorrow I will give, when you have it by you.

title: Book of Proverbs (Chapter 11, Verse 1)
text: A false balance is abomination to the LORD, but a just weight is his delight.

title: Book of Proverbs (Chapter 21, Verse 3)
text: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.

title: Book of Proverbs (Chapter 22, Verses 22–23)
text: Rob not the poor because he is poor, neither oppress the afflicted in the gate; for the LORD will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.

title: Temple Teacher near the Treasury: On Giving
text: Let no man give merely so that the sound of his coin may be heard. The Holy One sees the hand that gives, but he also weighs the heart. A small gift with humility is not small before Heaven.

title: Temple Teacher near the Western Gate: On Prayer
text: When you stand in this court and turn your face toward the sanctuary, turn also your heart toward the God of Israel. Lips may face west while the heart wanders far away; therefore gather your thoughts and pray with reverence.

title: Temple Teacher: On Sacrifice and Repentance
text: A man may bring a lamb without blemish, yet still keep deceit within his breast. Let him first cast away falsehood, anger, and oppression. Then his offering rises with a pleasing savor before the LORD.

title: Temple Teacher: On Purity before Entering the Courts
text: Consider where you stand. These are not the streets of the lower city, nor the marketplace, nor the gate of trade. Let each man and woman be mindful of purity, reverence, and modesty, for the courts of the LORD are holy.

title: Temple Teacher: On Justice in the Marketplace
text: What profit is there if a man prays in the morning and cheats with his measures at noon? The God who hears prayer also sees the balance, the weight, the ephah, and the hin. Let your trade be as clean as your offering.

title: Temple Teacher: On Speech
text: The tongue is small, yet it can wound a brother more sharply than iron. Do not carry slander through Jerusalem as a peddler carries wares. Speak truth, make peace, and do not shame your neighbor before others.

title: Temple Teacher: On Honoring Parents
text: The commandment says, Honor your father and your mother. Let no man bring gifts to the Temple while neglecting those who gave him life. The honor of parents is not less holy because it is practiced in the house.

title: Temple Teacher: On the Stranger
text: Remember that our fathers were strangers in Egypt. Therefore do not despise the stranger who comes near with reverence. The LORD loves justice, and he hears the cry of the one who has no protector.

title: Temple Teacher: On the Widow and the Orphan
text: If a widow is defrauded, if an orphan is pushed aside, do not say, Who will see it? The Judge of all the earth sees. Blessed is the man who strengthens the weak and does not turn his face from distress.

title: Temple Teacher: On Vows
text: Do not make a vow with a careless mouth. If you promise before the LORD, do not treat your words as wind. Better to speak little with faithfulness than much with deceit.

title: Temple Teacher: On Sabbath
text: The Sabbath is a sign between the LORD and Israel. Prepare for it with joy, keep it with honor, and do not turn rest into quarrel. A peaceful house honors the Sabbath more than a table filled with anger.

title: Temple Teacher: On Pilgrimage
text: You have come up to Jerusalem from towns and villages, from hill country and plain. Do not think the journey is fulfilled by your feet alone. Let your heart also ascend, from resentment to mercy, from pride to fear of Heaven.

title: Temple Teacher: On Humility in the Courts
text: Do not push forward as though nearness of body were nearness to God. The humble man standing far off may be nearer to Heaven than the proud man pressed against the gate.

title: Temple Teacher: On Teaching Children
text: Teach your children when you sit in your house and when you walk by the way. Let them know why Israel comes up to this mountain, why offerings are brought, and why the name of the LORD is blessed from generation to generation.

title: Temple Teacher: On Peace among Brothers
text: If you come to pray and remember anger against your brother, seek peace. The Holy One delights when brothers dwell together in unity. A reconciled heart is a fitting companion to sacrifice.

title: Temple Teacher: On the Fear of God
text: The fear of God is not trembling only, but obedience. It is seen in honest speech, clean hands, modest steps, mercy to the poor, and reverence in the holy place.

title: Temple Teacher: On Rome and the Kingdoms of Men
text: Do not say, The nations are strong, therefore Heaven is silent. Kingdoms rise and kingdoms fall, but the LORD reigns forever. Let Israel be faithful, and let every man repent of evil.

title: Temple Teacher: On the Hope of Israel
text: The prophets have spoken of comfort for Zion and mercy for Israel. Yet comfort is not for the stiff-necked, but for those who return to the LORD. Seek him while he may be found, and walk in his commandments.

title: Temple Teacher: On True Wisdom
text: Who is wise? The one who hears correction before judgment comes. Who is strong? The one who rules his own anger. Who is rich? The one who gives thanks for his portion before the LORD.
